title: Initial current magnitude
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (1) must correctly calculate the initial current as 4 A using I = BLv/(R+r).

title: Initial current direction
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (1) must correctly state the current direction (e.g., from Q to P) using the right-hand rule or Lenz's law.

title: Joule heat on R
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (2) must correctly calculate the Joule heat dissipated in resistor R as 4.8 J.

title: Stopping distance
description: Essential: The student's answer for part (3) must correctly calculate the final stopping distance from line ab as 1.6 m.

title: Energy conservation reasoning
description: Important: The solution should apply energy conservation, stating that the rod's initial kinetic energy is fully converted into total Joule heat in the circuit.

title: Charge-momentum relationship
description: Important: The solution for part (3) should correctly relate the total charge flow to the change in momentum via the impulse-momentum theorem (BLq = mv).

title: Heat distribution ratio
description: Important: The solution for part (2) should correctly distribute the total Joule heat between R and r using the resistance ratio Q_R = Q_total * R/(R+r).

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The student's work demonstrates consistent use and conversion of units (m, s, T, Ω, etc.) throughout the calculations.

title: Sign error in force direction
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly assigns the direction of the magnetic force (e.g., stating it accelerates the rod) or misapplies Lenz's law for current direction.

title: Ohm's law misapplication
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student uses an incorrect equivalent resistance (e.g., omitting the rod's resistance r) when calculating current or heat distribution.
